title: India floats AI plan under which ‘The model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model’
body:
The scheme India’s Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) thinks can make that happen is called the “Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI Training.”

As described by Professor Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, DEPA means “the model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model.” [...] MeitY’s DEPA framework [PDF] says this scheme means “Differential privacy techniques are systematically applied to prevent the model from learning or revealing individual specific information,” adding “All activities inside the secure data environments are immutably logged for audit purposes, ensuring that the process is both secure and transparent.”

India’s government already operates several data exchanges, but it is unclear how much work remains to make DEPA a reality. [...] It also makes several mentions of digital public infrastructure (DPI), an idea pioneered by India that involves government funding creation of tools like the Unified Payments Interface payment systems and the Bharat Taxi zero-commission ride-sharing platform, to ensure Big Tech companies don’t dominate the local market.

India also uses its DPI as a diplomatic tool, by giving it away to friendly nations. ®

title: Freshworks to acquire Israeli startup Torii to help companies control AI costs | Ctech
body: The acquisition will extend Freshworks’ Freshservice platform into software management and AI spending governance. The companies say the combination will give organizations a centralized view of their technology inventory, usage and spending, rather than requiring them to rely on separate systems. [...] Haramati said the acquisition would help address the fragmented view of software and AI usage across IT, finance and security teams. “AI and the software behind it are changing how every team works, and most CIOs still can't see it, let alone control it,” he said. “We built Torii because IT, finance, and security were each working off a different partial picture of the same problem. Freshservice already gives IT one system of record for everything it runs. Extending that to software and AI [...] Torii has raised $65 million in funding.
